identity: University of Amsterdam full-time Dutch Scandinavian Languages and Cultures BA, RIO 56807, formal Scandinavia Studies track, Danish main language, 2026–2027 ordinary curriculum.
controllingSources: Adopted programme OER B1, B2, B4, B5 and Appendix 1, dated curriculum 40883 and linked individual course entries. Faculty A6.4/A6.6 supplies the ordinary full-time 48 EC positive-BSA threshold.
components: The first year also requires a Dutch writing diagnostic. Tutoring and study guidance continue throughout the programme. These requirements carry no credits.
The Human World: Introduction to the Humanities
A World of Regions: Introduction to Area Studies
From Yggdrasil to Urban Slang: Languages of the North
Attend Danish 1–3 before this course. The Vikings course then requires attendance in Danish 1–4 and Modern Scandinavia.
Danish Language Proficiency 1 and Modern Denmark
This example uses Danish as the main language. Norwegian and Swedish are alternative main-language choices.
Danish Language Proficiency 2 and Modern Denmark
Danish Language Proficiency 3: Danish Culture, History and Society A
Complete Danish 2 before Danish 3. The language sequence also develops knowledge of Danish history, culture and contemporary society.
Danish Language Proficiency 4: Danish Culture, History and Society B
Complete the first-year Danish route before this course. It studies nineteenth- to twenty-first-century poetry, fiction and other literary texts in Danish.
Danish Language Proficiency 5 and Receptive Norwegian and Swedish
Pass Danish 4 before Danish 5. This unit also develops reading and listening in Norwegian and Swedish.
Philosophy of Science: National Identity, Borders and Territory

This example uses Copenhagen, the first Danish destination in the exchange course list. Complete at least 54 first-year EC and attend the first semester of year two before departure. The 30 EC must follow programme subject lines in cultural history, language/translation or literature; Danish, Norwegian and Swedish language-proficiency courses cannot count. A home alternative requires Examination Board approval.
Complete the earlier language preparation, including Danish 5 and receptive-language study, and Languages of the North before this research project.
Complete Danish 1–5 before translation. The course combines Danish-to-Dutch practice, source-text analysis, translation theory and Danish creative writing.

Use this 30 EC for electives, a minor, a placement or approved study abroad. Normally no more than 12 EC may be introductory; an approved UvA minor or same-language sequence can permit up to 24 EC. External study needs Examination Board approval. Placements can occupy at most 12 EC, and minors must not duplicate the required language study.

Complete the first year and at least 54 second-year EC before starting the thesis. A January workshop develops the proposal. The thesis is 8,000–10,000 words on a Scandinavian regional, linguistic, literary or cultural topic within available supervisory expertise. It is written in a Scandinavian language if assessed writing proficiency reaches B2/C1 or above; otherwise it is written in Dutch.

routeSelection: Danish is first in the dated guide’s Danish/Norwegian/Swedish list and is the complete retained route, independent of UCR fit. The detailed exchange course lists Copenhagen before Aarhus; Copenhagen is the first compatible Danish host. The introductory page’s different destination order does not override the detailed course. Host course titles are not invented: 30 EC must be approved within the specified regional subject lines.
sourceResolution: The public overview contains a generic paragraph describing an optional third-year stay. The adopted Appendix 1 and dated ordinary programme instead require the 30 EC second-year block. Course 57868 confirms its second-semester timing, subject rules and exceptional home alternative. The adopted version controls; no second exchange, home alternative or other main language is stacked. Parent totals include mutually exclusive language branches and are not summed as degree credits.
definingSubstance: OER B2 defines Scandinavian regional expertise through language, literary/cultural history especially from the nineteenth century onward, source analysis and humanities research. Modern Scandinavia covers industrialisation, democratisation, family/gender, Denmark–Greenland colonial relations, socio-economic policy and cultural representation. Rewriting the North adds Baltic geopolitics, Arctic appropriation, Sami/Inuit relations, discourse, memory and Indigenous methods. Languages of the North and the sociolinguistic project study linguistic relationships and variation in that region. Danish literature uses nineteenth- to twenty-first-century sources in Danish; regional identity and translation continue this subject-specific inquiry.

progression.yearOne: Four 6 EC Danish courses plus 36 common EC. Attend 1 before 2; complete 2 before 3 under the stricter entry wording; attend 3 before 4. Languages of the North requires prior attendance in 1–3, and Vikings requires 1–4 plus Modern Scandinavia. Their actual periods permit this order. Diagnostic writing and recurring tutoring carry zero credits.
progression.yearTwo: Complete the first year for Danish Literature; Danish 5 requires Danish 4 passed and the Danish propaedeutic language preparation. Its 6 EC includes 3 EC Danish and 1.5 EC each receptive Norwegian/Swedish, not additional credits. Positive BSA gates postpropaedeutic study. Exchange preparation is at least 54 first-year EC and attendance in the first semester of year two; this pathway completes year one and all four first-semester units. The 30 EC abroad may cover cultural history, language/translation and literature, plus approved Old Norse, Icelandic or Finnish, but excludes Danish/Norwegian/Swedish proficiency courses. The final 6 EC sociolinguistic project requires language courses 1–5 including receptive study and Languages of the North, all met beforehand.
progression.yearThree: Translation requires Danish 1–5 completed; Danish Literature is recommended. Rewriting the North and the Scandinavian group of National Identities in Europe build on receptive language skills and regional study. The 12 EC thesis requires the completed first year plus at least 54 second-year EC; completing all 60 second-year EC meets it. The January proposal workshop is not an extra credit unit. The thesis is 8,000–10,000 words in a Scandinavian regional, linguistic, literary or cultural field within available expertise. A language teacher assesses the Scandinavian-language proposal: sufficiently high B2/C1 writing permits a Scandinavian-language thesis, otherwise Dutch is used with stricter language assessment.
progression.freeChoice: The separate 30 EC group remains generic. OER B5 limits introductory study to 12 EC ordinarily or 24 in its stated UvA-minor/same-language exceptions. External courses/minors need Board approval. Danish and Dutch minors overlapping the Danish compulsory route are excluded. Placement is optional inside open space, at most 12 EC, not an extra mandatory element.
